behaviours.name: capture.body_is_non_vacuous
behaviours.what: capture bodies from profiles, commands and loaded records are absent or contain visible content, never blank or invisible placeholders

behaviours.name: capture.writer_staging_is_not_a_record
behaviours.what: the strict capture loader ignores only the guarded writer's exact canonical staging-file pattern while continuing to reject every other non-record inbox member

behaviours.name: capture.inbox_lifecycle_commands
behaviours.what: the inbox command provides focused show, open-only amendment, discard and discarded-only restore over one guarded capture snapshot

behaviours.name: capture.promotion_is_atomic
behaviours.what: inbox promotion creates one ordinary validated task and freezes its capture link in one retry-safe guarded transaction whose late failure rolls back every write

behaviours.name: tui.capture_forms_are_record_bound
behaviours.what: every native TUI form populated from a retained capture carries that record's immutable fingerprint and refuses preview if the capture changes or the visible id is redirected before review

behaviours.name: claim.uses_worktree_shared_ephemeral_state
behaviours.what: `claim` records time, origin and identity-source attribution in private local state shared by every linked worktree, while durable task `owner` remains stable

behaviours.name: claim.concurrent_disjoint_updates_compose
behaviours.what: concurrent claims or releases for different tasks retry guarded whole-store contention so every nonconflicting update is retained

behaviours.name: storage.atomic_replacement_is_portable
behaviours.what: guarded mutations and private cache refreshes retry transient Windows sharing denials while retaining the same atomic replacement and stale-input boundaries

behaviours.name: evidence.provider_executable_resolution_is_portable
behaviours.what: provider material identity resolves configured executables with the same native spelling accepted by process launch, including Windows' implicit `.exe` suffix

behaviours.name: coordination.is_not_a_plan_verdict_mutation
behaviours.what: `claim` and `release` mutate only local ephemeral coordination state, so they do not accept plan-verdict overrides or imply that the plan passed a gate

behaviours.name: release.recovers_orphaned_local_claims
behaviours.what: `release` can explicitly clear an ephemeral claim whose task is absent, while corrupt, unsafe or other orphaned claim state is never treated as free work

behaviours.name: owner.remains_stable_responsibility
behaviours.what: task `owner` is durable responsibility and claim or release never rewrites it

behaviours.name: owner.refuses_vacuous_values
behaviours.what: task creation and supersession refuse an owner made only of whitespace or invisible formatting characters rather than writing responsibility nobody can see

behaviours.name: selection.unclaimed_uses_ephemeral_claims
behaviours.what: `--unclaimed` selects the absence of an observed ephemeral claim, independently of durable `owner`, and refuses when local coordination is unavailable

behaviours.name: ready.exposes_ephemeral_claims
behaviours.what: `ready` and `aplan_ready` expose stable owner plus one local claim snapshot with holder, time, origin and explicit coordination scope

behaviours.name: show.exposes_ephemeral_claims
behaviours.what: `show` and `aplan_show` report stable owner and ephemeral claim as distinct facts, including claim age, origin and coordination scope

behaviours.name: stale.exposes_ephemeral_claims
behaviours.what: `stale` reports stable owner plus claim age and origin without a claim refreshing the task-file clock used to find neglected work

behaviours.name: tasks.exposes_ephemeral_claims
behaviours.what: `tasks --format json` carries the same explicit coordination scope and complete per-task claim records as the other read surfaces

behaviours.name: tui.distinguishes_owner_and_ephemeral_claim
behaviours.what: the TUI task list and inspector display the active local claim separately from durable task owner, including age, source, origin and unavailable coordination

behaviours.name: start.reports_ephemeral_holder
behaviours.what: `start` reports the ephemeral holder from local claim state rather than treating durable `owner` as the actor working now

behaviours.name: rekey.refuses_claimed_task
behaviours.what: `rekey` refuses an id carrying a local claim until it is explicitly released, so the old claim cannot become orphaned while the new id looks free

behaviours.name: claim.warns_on_placeholder_identity
behaviours.what: `claim` retains deterministic identity precedence but warns when the winning unauthenticated label looks like a machine or test placeholder

behaviours.name: claim.warns_on_cross_origin_identity_collision
behaviours.what: a holder label already observed from another local worktree origin produces an actionable warning that separate actors need distinct labels

behaviours.name: claim.origin_fallback_skips_invalid_host_values
behaviours.what: claim-origin attribution uses the first valid configured host label rather than letting a blank, overlong or control-bearing primary value suppress a valid fallback

behaviours.name: input_identity.uses_typed_canonical_bytes
behaviours.what: application input identities encode validation policy, verdict, configuration, paths, document state and explicit absence as deterministic typed bytes rather than Rust Debug output or map iteration order

behaviours.name: evidence.commit_requires_head_reachability
behaviours.what: APLAN011 accepts a commit citation only when its immutable SHA resolves to HEAD or one of HEAD's ancestors; APLAN012 and secondary commit rules never use an unreachable object, while incomplete shallow ancestry remains a checkout fault

behaviours.name: check_docs.identifier_boundaries_are_symmetric
behaviours.what: `check-docs` applies one Unicode-aware word-continuation predicate at both ends of ordinary, dotted, suffix-bearing and near-prefix task references

behaviours.name: check_docs.near_prefixes_prefer_longest_family
behaviours.what: `check-docs` matches overlapping one-digit-typo families longest-first, so the finding retains the complete referenced id and recommends the exact source family

behaviours.name: check_docs.complete_multi_hyphen_ids
behaviours.what: `check-docs` learns when a numeric id family carries hyphen-separated suffixes, resolves known complete ids and reports an unknown sibling without truncating it

behaviours.name: formats.refusal_names_every_rendered_surface
behaviours.what: a rejected known format describes every kind of output it can render and names the commands that accept it, rather than attributing its first surface to all of them

behaviours.name: tui.task_browser_preserves_selector_semantics
behaviours.what: the TUI task browser searches ids and titles, applies every shared selector dimension without changing plan semantics, exposes deterministic ready ranking, and preserves task identity across narrowing and refresh

behaviours.name: tui.task_browser_state_is_refresh_and_repeat_safe
behaviours.what: the TUI task browser applies enhanced-keyboard repeats to search editing without repeating modal activation, clamps a filter cursor after refresh, and anchors a hidden task identity at the visible viewport start

behaviours.name: show.carries_complete_task_projection
behaviours.what: the canonical typed `show` projection carries every persisted relationship, fingerprint and version claim, distinguishes missing from unloadable neighbours, and can include a body from the same identified input

behaviours.name: show.evidence_observations_are_nonblocking
behaviours.what: ordinary CLI and MCP task inspection never starts a configured provider and exposes typed per-citation and aggregate observation freshness; explicit bounded refresh recomputes the current plan against complete raw catalogues, reports exact runner progress, publishes only stable complete observations, and rejects stale late results

behaviours.name: evidence.scheduled_runner_identity_is_configured
behaviours.what: bounded provider discovery attributes catalogue rows, diagnostics and cost subjects to the same configured runner even when several runners have no name or directory label

behaviours.name: evidence.stale_premise_uses_configured_roots
behaviours.what: APLAN045 makes configured absolute plan paths repository-relative and resolves historical traced-document bytes through the configured trace root on `verify`, `show` and `aplan_show`

behaviours.name: tui.task_inspector_uses_show_projection
behaviours.what: the TUI task inspector searches task bodies, separates summary, body, relationships, paths, traces, evidence and findings from canonical `show`, wraps and scrolls inert text, preserves context through section and task links, and discards stale inspector coordinates when its snapshot refreshes

behaviours.name: tui.work_discovery_is_one_typed_flow
behaviours.what: the TUI joins ready rank factors and declared preferences, cut-bounded or complete why answers, and revisit due state at an explicit clock in one typed task inspector; due never claims an external condition is satisfied, and every loaded blocker or dependent is navigable with an identity-preserving back stack

behaviours.name: tui.work_discovery_state_is_semantically_exact
behaviours.what: the TUI canonicalizes a blank work clock so it follows refreshed snapshot time, keeps an explicit clock pinned, attributes an inactive preference to the exact unavailable side, and proves folded why and revisit controls against real data

behaviours.name: tui.overview_is_one_typed_projection
behaviours.what: the TUI Overview renders plan, build and refresh identity plus cut, effort, ready, due, finding and critical-path values from one typed projection, preserves honest empty and partial states, and drills each aggregate into the exact identities that produced it

behaviours.name: tui.overview_revisit_membership_is_exact
behaviours.what: the TUI Overview retains distinct timestamped identities for due and future revisits, and opening the composite row re-projects every task counted by both sides from the current snapshot

behaviours.name: tui.diagnostic_workbench_retains_complete_runs
behaviours.what: the TUI retains structural and configured-document diagnostics as distinct complete runs with independent verdicts, exact ordered findings and stable identities; filtering and grouping preserve canonical order and cannot turn a partial or denied run into a clean verdict, while detail carries subject, location, instruction, contribution and safe source context

behaviours.name: tui.narrowed_diagnostic_state_is_truthful
behaviours.what: an active diagnostic search or filter is always disclosed, an empty narrowed view names the retained whole-run verdict instead of claiming the run is clean, and narrowing and one-run relaxation remain visible before truncatable metadata

behaviours.name: tui.check_overrides_are_one_run
behaviours.what: the TUI advanced check sheet exposes effective effort, trace and warning policy, carries explicit overrides on one effect request, labels a relaxed result, and restores repository policy for the next ordinary refresh

behaviours.name: tui.verification_is_typed_and_non_blocking
behaviours.what: the TUI reviews identified repository, policy and provider inputs before running verification on its bounded worker; execute is explicit, complete findings and per-citation strength, outcome, detail and shared cost stay typed, exact repairs remain inspect-only, and queued, running, completed, refused, timed-out, output-limited, unavailable and stale states cannot impersonate one another

behaviours.name: tui.verification_execution_is_preview_bound
behaviours.what: interactive verification reloads and compares the reviewed input before any configured provider can run, reports a mismatch as typed stale work, and derives the evidence repository solely from the identified application context

behaviours.name: tui.evidence_mutation_previews_bind_identified_inputs
behaviours.what: interactive close, amend, restamp and verification repair work is staged as one typed guarded ChangeSet whose evidence ledger and policy are inspectable, and publication re-observes its identified plan, repository HEAD/status and selected configuration inputs

behaviours.name: tui.work_preview_responses_are_request_bound
behaviours.what: an interactive work preview derives its action and review projection from the immutable typed request and can replace a form only when its request token, selected task and identified plan input still match the unchanged form

behaviours.name: tui.mutation_layers_do_not_adopt_prior_effects
behaviours.what: after a running mutation layer is dismissed, another mutation cannot open until the prior effect finishes, and that late result is discarded without creating or populating a new layer

behaviours.name: tui.authoring_capture_refuses_non_regular_before_blocking
behaviours.what: interactive manifest and import capture accepts only a bounded regular file and refuses a stream or device before opening it can block the mutation worker, including a regular-file-to-FIFO replacement race on Unix

behaviours.name: tui.configured_test_selector_is_reachable
behaviours.what: the TUI command palette starts configured-test discovery on the bounded worker, retains partial and ambiguous resolver advice, searches the typed answer locally, and inserts only an unambiguous exact reference into the selected task's close or amend form

behaviours.name: tui.planning_forms_render_typed_choice_context
behaviours.what: interactive dependency and preference forms render the complete typed endpoint catalogue with status, cut membership and current-edge state while excluding self; tag forms render declared family scope, cardinality, members, selected values and observed arbitrary tags before preview

behaviours.name: tui.broad_mutations_are_recoverable
behaviours.what: broad interactive mutations enumerate every affected task and file, bind exact plan and selected-configuration bytes, require a deliberately re-focused confirmation, retain form input and per-path unchanged/complete/diverged observations after failure, and report success only after a fresh snapshot contains the reviewed after-state

behaviours.name: tui.mutation_surface_has_cross_adapter_parity
behaviours.what: the interactive mutation catalogue is a closed-world union of typed workflows; task/plan CLI modes are mapped or visibly bounded, representative coordination, planning, authoring and evidence writes cross a real PTY review boundary, and shared CLI, MCP and TUI requests retain exact post-state and refusal parity

behaviours.name: tui.graph_explorer_uses_semantic_scene
behaviours.what: the TUI graph explorer composes shared selectors with core reach, tree and critical-path scopes over the canonical typed GraphView, paints only visible ranges of the CLI's semantic scene, preserves exact omissions and identities, and supports non-colour selection, relationship following, hit testing, panning and recentering

behaviours.name: tui.graph_context_discloses_scope_and_grouping_omissions
behaviours.what: the TUI graph context names the relation class its active structural scope actually walked and reports exact omitted cut-membership-edge and grouping-only-task counts at every supported width

behaviours.name: tui.graph_windows_are_bounded_and_accounted
behaviours.what: the application projects selector/scope/membership results into deterministic anchor-preserving node, edge and lane budgets; exact omissions, cyclic/empty/failed states and paged incoming, outgoing and disconnected-component continuations stay typed, stable and reachable without changing complete CLI graph output

behaviours.name: tui.graph_explorer_projects_multiscale_semantics
behaviours.what: the application projects plan, phase, milestone and task levels from one admitted canonical task graph; phase remains grouping, milestone edges retain every underlying dependency and quotient feedback stays distinct from invalid task cycles, while raw selection, exact accounting, bounded task continuations and reversible transitions remain source-bound

behaviours.name: tui.graph_window_cursors_are_source_bound
behaviours.what: every graph continuation cursor carries the immutable input identity which emitted it, and a cursor presented to a refreshed or otherwise different projection is refused as invalid rather than reinterpreted by ordinal position

behaviours.name: tui.graph_explorer_windows_oversized_inputs
behaviours.what: the TUI opens an oversized graph as an explicitly labelled, fully accounted semantic window; keyboard and pointer controls traverse and reverse source-bound continuations, relationship navigation recentres omitted identities, neighbourhood depth composes with structural scope, and resizing changes only presentation

behaviours.name: tui.report_hub_preserves_cli_report_semantics
behaviours.what: the TUI report hub retains typed roadmap, summary, version, paths, vacuity, stale and deprecation values, states computation scope explicitly, and drills a row's frozen contributors without recomputing the report

behaviours.name: tui.report_discovery_is_literal_and_parameter_safe
behaviours.what: the TUI searches report names and typed result rows without changing report scope, edits the stale as-of date through a distinct contextual action, and displays configured version-source argv without erasing argument boundaries

behaviours.name: tui.external_refresh_is_identity_safe
behaviours.what: the TUI identifies plan, configuration, HEAD and exact Git status inputs, probes them off the input thread, atomically rejects a refresh raced by a newer identity, and preserves identity-based navigation while the previous complete snapshot remains visible

behaviours.name: tui.focus_epoch_invalidates_external_results
behaviours.what: a probe or refresh requested before terminal focus is lost cannot certify a later active focus epoch, and regaining focus obtains a current-epoch observation

behaviours.name: tui.suspension_invalidates_snapshot_freshness
behaviours.what: process suspension advances the external-observation epoch before stopping, resume paints retained bytes as unconfirmed and obtains a current-epoch observation as soon as worker capacity is available

behaviours.name: tui.continue_cancels_pending_suspend_handoff
behaviours.what: a continue observed after terminal teardown cancels a pending suspend decision before the default stop handler can strand the process, without changing quit or termination results

behaviours.name: tui.continue_establishes_freshness_boundary
behaviours.what: every continue that resumes interactive work establishes an external-observation boundary, including a standalone continue after an uncatchable stop and a continue that cancels the post-teardown suspend handoff

behaviours.name: tui.overdue_external_probe_is_fail_closed
behaviours.what: a periodic identity probe that cannot start because the bounded worker is occupied makes snapshot freshness unconfirmed and remains due until capacity starts it

behaviours.name: tui.quit_starts_no_new_work
behaviours.what: after input requests quit, termination and suspension retain precedence while continue is inert; the TUI exits before draining a completion that could start queued work, starting a probe, drawing another frame or polling for more input

behaviours.name: tui.production_external_probe_avoids_refresh_work
behaviours.what: periodic and focus-gain probes load the complete production input identity without constructing refresh-only verification or report projections, while refresh confirmation uses the same identity observation

behaviours.name: graph.merge_starts_at_destination_lane
behaviours.what: a fan-in merge begins at its destination lane, preserving unrelated routes to its left as vertical cells with only their own edge identities

behaviours.name: graph.text_focus_and_critical_overlay
behaviours.what: `graph --format text` retains the canonical semantic scene while adding exact statuses, a focus with visible direct dependency neighbours, the deterministic whole-plan critical route and exact edge cues through documented non-colour badges and stream-resolved terminal styling; presentation never changes scope or machine formats

behaviours.name: graph.critical_visibility_counts_step_identities
behaviours.what: the CLI text graph counts visible critical-route step identities rather than matching scene edge records, so repeated equal endpoints count once and omitted edges count zero

behaviours.name: summary.revision_selects_committed_inputs
behaviours.what: `summary --at` reads the plan and its discovered configuration from one resolved commit without a checkout, while an explicit configuration remains selected

behaviours.name: summary.revision_uses_historical_repository_boundary
behaviours.what: `summary --at` assigns an explicit in-repository root to the invocation's historical tree, unaffected by nested repositories created later, and refuses a plan-root gitlink or broken root link as incomplete input while accepting a root link to the top tree; an external repository, including one reached through an alias, requires the caller to select or decline current policy explicitly

behaviours.name: attest.note_targets_attested_commit
behaviours.what: an attached attestation is written to the exact commit recorded in its document, even if HEAD advances before the note write

behaviours.name: verify.url_checker_outcomes_are_stable
behaviours.what: each url's answered, refused or timed-out outcome is checked once and reused for every citation; a checker crash is one configuration fault and cannot erase an earlier answer

behaviours.name: selection.phase_coordinate
behaviours.what: the repeatable phase coordinate narrows every selecting command and may scope policy through the same selector without changing graph or readiness semantics

behaviours.name: export.checklist_names_single_phase_loss
behaviours.what: checklist export reports phase loss for every non-empty export and gives a single-phase plan the exact import flag that preserves its value

behaviours.name: config.grouping_error_names_its_view
behaviours.what: an undeclared family in `roadmap.group_by` or `summary.group_by` is refused as invalid grouping and names the exact view key, never the test runner

behaviours.name: config.tag_family_error_names_its_key
behaviours.what: a structurally invalid `tag_families` declaration is refused as that exact configuration block, never as an invalid test runner

behaviours.name: summary.grouped_human_is_unambiguous
behaviours.what: a grouped human summary names its family, renders every member distinctly from synthetic rows, and aligns values by terminal display width

behaviours.name: diagnostics.machine_applicable_repairs
behaviours.what: diagnostics carry exact evidence replacements as typed data, and `verify --fix` applies all valid ones as one guarded mutation before verifying the result

behaviours.name: diagnostics.repair_requires_unique_resolver
behaviours.what: a typed test-name repair is published only when exactly one configured runner resolves its replacement; a shared spelling remains prose advice

behaviours.name: evidence.test_unresolved_points_to_catalogue
behaviours.what: an unresolved or ambiguous test citation points at `aplan test list`, which exposes the resolver's exact configured names and runner identities

behaviours.name: verify_fix.post_runner_plan_is_gated
behaviours.what: `verify --fix` reloads the whole plan after configured runners finish, refuses their newly invalid sibling state before writing, and preserves valid sibling edits

behaviours.name: verify_fix.post_runner_config_is_gated
behaviours.what: `verify --fix` reloads the selected configuration after external resolvers finish and validates every replacement under the policy its post-verification will use

behaviours.name: verify_fix.one_post_runner_config_source
behaviours.what: `verify --fix` uses the post-run configuration discovered from its evidence repository for replacement resolution, mutation gating, and post-verification

behaviours.name: rollup.cut_excludes_releases
behaviours.what: a task's reported `cut` is the cut it is in, never a release that closes it

behaviours.name: verify_fix.revalidation_side_effects_are_gated
behaviours.what: `verify --fix` builds its candidate from the plan left by every replacement resolver and refuses a configuration that changes during that validation

behaviours.name: traces.table_rows
behaviours.what: a `traces` anchor may name a table row by its first cell

behaviours.name: verdict.summary_agrees_with_exit_code
behaviours.what: the `ok`/`failed` word and the reported counts are what blocked, not every finding

behaviours.name: ready.order_is_derived
behaviours.what: `ready` answers in a derived rank (what a task releases, then the critical path, then the chain of work behind it, then effort) rather than in id order, and `--explain` says which

behaviours.name: paths.unmatched_needs_evidence
behaviours.what: `APLAN019` reports a dead `paths` glob only where the task cites a `commit`, `file` or `test`, so a plan that names trees a later cut creates is silent

behaviours.name: paths.unmatched_ignores_a_bound_sibling
behaviours.what: `APLAN019` is silent about a dead `paths` glob when the task's cited commit or file binds through another one, so a stale declaration does not refuse a close

behaviours.name: paths.unmatched_ignores_vacuous_evidence
behaviours.what: `APLAN019` names only substantive commit, file and test references in its diagnostic, using the same invisible-reference predicate that scopes the rule

behaviours.name: evidence.vacuous_test_does_not_acquit_dilution
behaviours.what: `APLAN024` does not accept a whitespace-only or invisible test reference as independent proof that acquits diluted commit evidence

behaviours.name: evidence.batch_outcomes_preserve_terminal_semantics
behaviours.what: the existing test-batch result protocol keeps expected failure, retry, flake, cancellation, timeout, resource, framework and incomplete outcomes distinct, and a retry-created green cannot be encoded as an unconditional pass

behaviours.name: evidence.portable_provider_receipts
behaviours.what: `test receipt` exports one complete provider execution as a canonical, plan-independent statement whose current material and externally authenticated producer can be validated before it is used as evidence

behaviours.name: evidence.receipt_backed_whole_plan_resolution
behaviours.what: `verify --test-receipts` authenticates one complete current observation per configured provider, recomputes the exact current whole-plan L1/L2/L3 verdict, and never starts a test provider or silently falls back to direct execution

behaviours.name: evidence.verification_reports_provider_provenance
behaviours.what: human, JSON, MCP and TUI verification results identify observation scope, provider source, freshness and completeness without conflating receipt, direct and deferred work

behaviours.name: evidence.incremental_receipt_refresh
behaviours.what: `verify --refresh-test-receipts` derives invalidation from an explicit Git boundary, executes only identities covered by an exhaustive input-dependency declaration, widens every ambiguous case, atomically publishes a complete current receipt set, and re-derives the whole-plan verdict

behaviours.name: ready.reports_a_closeable_cut
behaviours.what: `ready` names a cut whose members are all done rather than answering with silence

behaviours.name: mutation.refused_when_check_would_reject
behaviours.what: a command or tool that writes runs the rules against the plan it would produce, and refuses a mutation that introduces a finding

behaviours.name: dep.rebases_on_current_target
behaviours.what: a dependency edit derives its relationship list and mutation verdict from the current task bytes, preserving a valid edge added after its read snapshot

behaviours.name: dep.preserves_scalar_sequence_source_deltas
behaviours.what: dependency and preference edge edits retain the exact source of surviving scalar sequence members and surrounding trivia, and refuse a structure they cannot edit unambiguously instead of rebuilding it

behaviours.name: tag.preserves_scalar_sequence_source_deltas
behaviours.what: tag add, remove and plan-wide rename retain the exact source of surviving scalar sequence members and surrounding trivia, and refuse a structural sequence they cannot edit unambiguously without changing another field

behaviours.name: application.input_identity_matches_loaded_inputs
behaviours.what: an application result's input identity is derived from the exact candidate bytes parsed for that result, including Markdown candidates that are not yet tasks

behaviours.name: verify.one_tasks_defect_does_not_stop_the_run
behaviours.what: a defect in one task's input, or in one configured command, is a finding rather than a reason to abandon the run and report nothing about the rest

behaviours.name: verify.configured_commands_are_bounded
behaviours.what: a configured `test.list` or `url.check` that does not return is killed at its limit and reported, rather than waited for

behaviours.name: cli.configured_commands_follow_termination_signals
behaviours.what: on Unix, every non-interactive CLI path closes configured-command startup, stops all active process groups and preserves SIGINT, SIGTERM, SIGHUP or SIGQUIT as the caller-visible outcome

behaviours.name: ready.honours_a_declared_preference
behaviours.what: `ready` offers a task after the offered tasks its `prefer_after` names, without ever blocking it

behaviours.name: milestone.members_are_live_work
behaviours.what: `APLAN021` counts a cut's members as live work, so a cut left holding only other cuts, or only cancelled tasks, is reported rather than silent

behaviours.name: cut.named_by_id_or_label
behaviours.what: a `--cut` argument may be the milestone id or the label the cut reports itself under, on every command that takes one

behaviours.name: supersede.successor_is_placed_and_classified
behaviours.what: a successor inherits the predecessor's subject tags and is judged in the cut `--cut` names, so `supersede` itself can repair a plan that requires a tag family and a cut membership

behaviours.name: supersede.controls_inherited_successor_content
behaviours.what: `supersede` inherits paths, traces and its generated body only when their controls are omitted; explicit replacements, clears and a supplied body publish atomically

behaviours.name: import.carries_the_plans_vocabulary
behaviours.what: `import` gives every task it writes the tags the invocation names, and says which declared `tag_families` member the import would otherwise leave missing, so a plan with a mandatory vocabulary can be imported into

behaviours.name: milestone.release_holds_cuts
behaviours.what: a milestone tagged `release` holds the cuts it closes: `APLAN021` accepts it and `roadmap` rolls up their work rather than reporting none

behaviours.name: rollup.carries_effort
behaviours.what: `roadmap` and `summary` report the effort behind their counts, and divide it into weeks where `effort_days_per_week` is declared

behaviours.name: config.explicitly_selectable
behaviours.what: `--config <file>` reads exactly that file and discovers none, `--no-config` reads none at all, and a named file that is missing is an error rather than a fallback

behaviours.name: traces.boundary_is_plan_repository
behaviours.what: `APLAN034` judges a trace against the plan's repository even when `--config` selects policy elsewhere; config-relative values and diagnostic locations stay with the selected file

behaviours.name: close.evidence_resolves_before_write
behaviours.what: `close` resolves a proposed citation before it writes, on both surfaces; only `--no-resolve` opts out, and it says what it skipped

behaviours.name: close.focused_l3_is_explicit_scoped_and_stale_safe
behaviours.what: `close --execute` explicitly runs only the proposed closure's distinct test identities, requires typed L3 passes, and publishes the reviewed task only while plan, repository, configuration and selected provider material remain current; ordinary close and agent tools remain L2-only

behaviours.name: close.focused_l3_terminal_outcomes_name_external_effects
behaviours.what: every focused L3 outcome after configured test code starts distinguishes aplan's guarded plan publication from command effects it cannot roll back, on CLI and interactive surfaces

behaviours.name: close.replaces_live_trace_fingerprints
behaviours.what: `close` replaces an accepted live task's existing trace fingerprint mapping in place with freshly resolved stamps instead of appending a duplicate key

behaviours.name: close.refuses_structural_fingerprint_mappings
behaviours.what: close, restamp and evidence repair replace ordinary block or one-line flow fingerprint maps, while structural mappings refuse actionably before any task bytes are written

behaviours.name: close.refuses_structural_evidence_sequences
behaviours.what: explicit and computed citation edits replace only an ordinary source-local block sequence of citation mappings; structural evidence refuses actionably before any task bytes or batch prefix are written

behaviours.name: amend.policy_reads_rewritten_evidence_candidate
behaviours.what: evidence amendment derives resolution, mutation-policy and freshness inputs by parsing the exact candidate produced by the core rewrite, so captured metadata cannot make a newly written citation look like an empty delta

behaviours.name: amend.preserves_evidence_sequence_source_deltas
behaviours.what: evidence add, remove and replace retain every unaddressed ordinary citation byte, including mapping indentation, key spacing, quote style, comments and newline convention, while structural sequences keep their exact no-write refusal

behaviours.name: close.preserves_fingerprint_mapping_boundary_trivia
behaviours.what: fingerprint replacement preserves an accepted ordinary mapping's literal key, colon spacing and boundary comment, retaining the comment standalone when the final derived baseline is cleared

behaviours.name: portfolio.preserves_rewrite_error_category
behaviours.what: park and unpark preserve typed rewrite failures through the CLI adapter, so plan input refusals exit as usage and a failed writer self-check exits as aplan's published internal error

behaviours.name: portfolio.refuses_alternate_optional_scalar_keys
behaviours.what: park and unpark edit ordinary revisit scalar lines exactly, while quoted or otherwise non-local optional-scalar keys refuse actionably before any target in the portfolio batch is written

behaviours.name: close.refuses_alternate_evidence_keys
behaviours.what: initial close treats every top-level key the YAML mapping resolves to `evidence` as an existing field, refusing a live task actionably and without constructing or writing a duplicate-key candidate

behaviours.name: close.refuses_empty_version_fields
behaviours.what: release close distinguishes an absent version field from every ordinary or alternate top-level key carrying a null value, refusing the present empty field actionably and without constructing or writing a duplicate-key candidate

behaviours.name: mutation.refuses_multiline_plain_scalar_rewrites
behaviours.what: line-local task scalar edits compare the complete parsed field with the inline source token, refusing multiline plain ids and optional values actionably before any task or batch bytes are written

behaviours.name: close.restamp_requires_drift_detection
behaviours.what: `close --restamp` refuses while `detect_drift` is disabled instead of claiming success while deleting trace and evidence baselines it did not refresh

behaviours.name: close.restamp_reports_baseline_changes
behaviours.what: `close --restamp` separately reports changed and already-current trace and committed file-evidence baselines, does not replace the task file when every baseline in its current task snapshot is current, and refuses a task changed since its plan load rather than misreporting a no-op

behaviours.name: mutation.block_replacements_cross_yaml_trivia
behaviours.what: surgical mapping and sequence replacements cross blank lines and comments without leaving an old entry behind or moving the trivia and following field

behaviours.name: paths.no_sample_is_not_a_zero
behaviours.what: `aplan paths` reports that nothing was sampled rather than a share of 0%, and a task whose `paths` do not compile is left unmeasured rather than counted as zero

behaviours.name: verify.reports_what_nothing_checked
behaviours.what: `verify` reports the citations its configuration gave it no resolver for, rather than counting them as resolved

behaviours.name: add.reads_a_task_list
behaviours.what: `aplan add --from <file>` adds every task a file names as one change, each entry resolved against the ones before it

behaviours.name: add.accepts_creation_time_model_fields
behaviours.what: single and manifest task creation author live state, scheduling, version impact and every declared relationship in one validated write, including relationships to later manifest entries

behaviours.name: dep.atomic_batch_rewrites
behaviours.what: dependency additions and removals are judged as one final graph and guarded publication, while add-from and blueprint reverse blocks edges to existing or same-batch tasks publish with creation

behaviours.name: add_from.resolves_terminal_ledger_entries_atomically
behaviours.what: a manifest may add proved done history to a done cut only after every citation resolves and trace/evidence baselines are captured, with any failure leaving the complete batch and cut unchanged

behaviours.name: authoring.refuses_visually_empty_creation_values
behaviours.what: single and manifest authoring refuse visually empty ids, titles, metadata, relationships and bodies before any file is written

behaviours.name: blueprint.parameters_bind_totally_after_parsing
behaviours.what: blueprint parameters bind every parameterisable typed string slot after YAML parsing, refuse missing, undeclared or unused names, and treat supplied values as opaque non-recursive text

behaviours.name: blueprint.references_resolve_atomically
behaviours.what: blueprint relationships use explicit `local:` and `task:` namespaces, resolve every sibling key to an id minted for one current plan snapshot, and publish the complete graph into one existing cut only when its post-state passes

behaviours.name: agent_contract.guides_explicit_blueprint_application
behaviours.what: the generated agent contract says when a recurring plan shape warrants a blueprint, gives the explicit-file dry-run command, and requires review of its source identity and complete predicted graph before application

behaviours.name: add.refuses_milestone_work_fields
behaviours.what: `aplan add` and `add --from` refuse a milestone carrying `effort` or `paths`, and write nothing, regardless of the warning policy

behaviours.name: add.milestone_work_refusal_is_new_input_only
behaviours.what: the unconditional milestone-work-field refusal applies only to a milestone this add creates; improving an existing malformed cut remains under warning policy

behaviours.name: add.creates_cut_around_existing_members
behaviours.what: `add --member`, native application/TUI add and `aplan_add` create an explicitly identified milestone around existing live work, remove every old membership and publish all files as one validated guarded batch

behaviours.name: mcp.add_accepts_explicit_identity
behaviours.what: ordinary `aplan_add` accepts an explicit task id and reporting phase, uses both verbatim and mints or derives them only when the caller omits them

behaviours.name: mcp.add_refuses_milestone_work_fields
behaviours.what: `aplan_add` refuses a new milestone carrying `effort_days` or `paths` before writing, under every warning policy, like both CLI add forms

behaviours.name: mcp.explicit_root_resolves_one_repository_context
behaviours.what: an explicit MCP root denotes either a repository carrying `.aplan.yml` or its configured plan directory, resolves plan, policy, traces, evidence providers and Git together, exposes bounded provenance and refuses a partial or ambiguous root without falling back to the server's launch repository

behaviours.name: mcp.launch_context_honours_trace_selection
behaviours.what: an MCP server's launch context honours configured `traces_root` and `no_traces` before applying its repository fallback

behaviours.name: evidence.file_path_is_normalised
behaviours.what: a path is read the same way wherever a plan writes one: a `file` citation, a `paths` glob and a `traces` target all resolve however it is spelled (`./x`, `a/../x`)

behaviours.name: evidence.file_names_a_section
behaviours.what: a `file` citation may name the section that proves it (`file:docs/report.md#result`), resolved against that document's own headings and table rows at the cited rev, so a written decision is citable as evidence rather than only as a file that exists

behaviours.name: facts.reports_which_build
behaviours.what: `aplan facts --identity` names this build -- its version, the commit it was built from, and the digests of its capability document and its own image -- without needing a plan, a repository or a clean tree

behaviours.name: facts.source_identity_tracks_active_checkout
behaviours.what: the build-time source identity ignores inherited `GIT_` context and follows the active checkout through loose refs, packed refs, disabled reflogs and linked worktrees without making ordinary unrelated branches build inputs

behaviours.name: facts.reports_build_capabilities
behaviours.what: `aplan facts` reports whether optional build capability `build.tui` is enabled, and `facts --require` accepts it only in a build that compiled the interface

behaviours.name: tui.cursor_restoration_is_singular
behaviours.what: `aplan tui` leaves cursor visibility to the Ratatui terminal, so a foundation frame and normal exit emit one hide and one restoring show rather than two competing pairs

behaviours.name: tui.event_loop_is_generation_safe
behaviours.what: `aplan tui` decodes terminal input into semantic actions, redraws only after state changes, and runs one identified effect with one bounded queued successor while stale or failed results cannot replace the last complete snapshot

behaviours.name: tui.caught_worker_panics_do_not_write_terminal
behaviours.what: a panic caught at the TUI effect-worker boundary becomes a typed failure without writing through the active terminal, while non-worker panics still reach the host's previous panic hook

behaviours.name: tui.worker_cleanup_is_unwind_safe
behaviours.what: dropping the TUI worker runtime, including during unwinding, cancels queued work and joins the sole running repository or process operation instead of detaching it

behaviours.name: tui.terminal_lifecycle_handles_signals
behaviours.what: every non-interactive command preserves its caller's terminal and emits only declared SGR controls; the TUI restores exact terminal state, stops active configured-command groups and re-raises catchable termination signals without waiting for the worker, while suspend restores before stopping and continue reacquires and repaints

behaviours.name: tui.terminal_portability_is_explicit
behaviours.what: a dedicated platform-neutral real-PTY module exercises mode ownership, focus, resize and minimum-size recovery plus ordinary and interrupt teardown, while the support matrix keeps unavailable platform observations distinct from passes

behaviours.name: tui.external_editor_handoff_is_safe_and_identity_bound
behaviours.what: the Add form launches VISUAL or EDITOR directly only after restoring terminal modes, accepts one private bounded Markdown draft through ordinary preview, and reacquires the interface only after requesting a current input observation

behaviours.name: tui.termination_preempts_worker_shutdown
behaviours.what: after restoring the terminal for a graceful quit, the TUI continues polling lifecycle signals while it waits for its worker, so catchable termination kills configured-command groups and preserves the signal exit instead of hanging

behaviours.name: tui.shell_is_responsive_and_contextual
behaviours.what: the TUI provides keyboard-complete routed wide, normal and narrow shells whose dispatch, footer, help and palette share one availability-aware command catalogue and whose text, cursor and hit targets use terminal-cell geometry

behaviours.name: tui.action_discovery_is_closed_and_contextual
behaviours.what: palette, full help and contextual footer consume one availability-aware action catalogue; every command published by facts maps to a driven native surface, guided route, inert exact CLI alternative or the TUI entry point, and every CLI leaf and semantic option has an executable disposition

behaviours.name: tui.modal_navigation_is_consistent
behaviours.what: arrow, j/k, Tab and Shift-Tab navigation all move and wrap the active modal selection instead of changing the obscured main view

behaviours.name: tui.selection_is_visible_and_pointer_safe
behaviours.what: the responsive TUI keeps selected task rows visible, derives painting and pointer targets from one bounded viewport, and preserves an escapable, size-bounded input surface across narrow and below-minimum layouts

behaviours.name: tui.shell_content_is_explicitly_bounded
behaviours.what: every responsive TUI surface fits hostile text to its real content rectangle with an explicit continuation marker, pointer targets stay inside painted cells, and wheel navigation stops at task-list boundaries

behaviours.name: tui.visual_language_is_semantic_and_deterministic
behaviours.what: the TUI resolves explicit dark, light, low-color and monochrome themes against NO_COLOR and reported color capacity without guessing a background; semantic roles, exact compact visualizations, ASCII equivalents and reduced-motion progress survive every responsive class

behaviours.name: tui.input_accessibility_is_safe_and_discoverable
behaviours.what: the TUI derives dispatch, quick help, complete help and palette key labels from one lifecycle-aware binding catalogue; keyboard-complete layers restore exact focus, and clamped pointer accelerators cannot click or wheel through an overlay or activate on drag, release or modifiers

behaviours.name: tui.overlay_pointer_activation_is_semantic_and_guarded
behaviours.what: visible modal rows, labelled overlay controls and mutation fields expose typed pointer targets derived from their painted geometry, while confirmation retains freshness, broad-change and pending-work guards

behaviours.name: tui.startup_feedback_precedes_plan_io
behaviours.what: an eligible interactive launch paints a responsive in-frame loading state before configuration or plan reads begin, consumes one generation-safe phase stream, and restores the terminal before reporting failure or joining cancelled work

behaviours.name: tui.inspectors_use_semantic_information_hierarchy
behaviours.what: task inspector sections carry typed identity, groups, labelled values, badges, metrics, callouts and links; wide panes align them and narrow panes stack the same exact values with non-colour meaning and stable selection

behaviours.name: tui.shell_adapts_by_route_and_available_rows
behaviours.what: the shell allocates chrome independently from pane width, retains route-specific useful work and explicit primary/detail orientation through short and narrow layouts, keeps hidden commands discoverable, and reflows without changing semantic or editable state

behaviours.name: tui.onboarding_and_capabilities_are_typed
behaviours.what: the TUI keeps missing, unreadable or invalid launch inputs in a read-only guided state, can retry into one complete snapshot, names root and configuration trust choices, and renders About from the same typed facts as `aplan facts`

behaviours.name: facts.omits_disabled_feature_behaviours
behaviours.what: `aplan facts` omits `tui.*` behaviour names when `build.tui` is disabled, so `--require` cannot accept a promise made only by code this build did not compile

behaviours.name: output.plan_text_cannot_steer_a_terminal
behaviours.what: a control character in any field a plan supplies is replaced by a visible marker before it reaches a human rendering, at every `--color` setting, while the machine formats keep the bytes the plan holds

behaviours.name: contract.begin_marker_matched_by_prefix
behaviours.what: the generated block's opening marker is recognised by its start: a line opening `<!-- aplan:begin`, then a space or a dash, and closing `-->`, which writing the block replaces with the full marker

behaviours.name: color.explicitly_selectable
behaviours.what: `--color=auto|always|never` overrides the terminal detection in both directions, reaching everything the tool prints -- its findings, its refusals, and `clap`'s own usage errors -- while the machine formats stay byte-identical at every setting

behaviours.name: progress.events_are_generation_safe
behaviours.what: plan loading and configured-provider work emit one ordered typed lifecycle whose operation generation, child identities and monotonic measures let a consumer reject late, duplicate, regressing or cross-operation events

behaviours.name: progress.stream_output_is_automation_safe
behaviours.what: operation progress is delayed and stderr-only; auto requires an attended human mode outside CI, always is explicit, never emits no progress bytes, machine stdout is unchanged and the TUI retains in-frame ownership

behaviours.name: progress.cli_renderer_is_identity_safe_and_terminal_safe
behaviours.what: one command-lifetime CLI renderer validates operation and child identities, aggregates bounded concurrent work, fits the terminal, serializes ordinary output and restores its transient row on success, failure, cancellation or catchable process interruption

behaviours.name: traces.structured_documents
behaviours.what: a `traces` anchor may address a node of a YAML or JSON document, as a JSON Pointer (`#/states/provisioning`) or a JSONPath (`#$.states.provisioning`)

behaviours.name: traces.unstamped_is_reported
behaviours.what: a `done` task that stamps none of its anchored `traces` is reported by `APLAN028`, rather than exempt as a task closed before drift was enabled

behaviours.name: generated.names_the_build_that_wrote_it
behaviours.what: a generated `ROADMAP.status.md` and `AGENTS.md` block carry a comment naming the version and surface that wrote them, and a drift report names the build doing the checking

behaviours.name: why.cut_bounded_by_default
behaviours.what: `aplan why` reports an unfinished cut as itself rather than walking into its members, and names the traversal that produced every answer; `--all` asks for the complete closure

behaviours.name: why.complete_retains_nested_undefined_blockers
behaviours.what: a complete why walk retains undefined blockers reached below loaded tasks on CLI, JSON and MCP, while a cut-bounded walk hides an undefined id behind its cut

behaviours.name: identity.reads_a_per_user_file
behaviours.what: a claimant's name may come from a per-user file outside the repository, read between the environment variable and git's `user.name`, and holding nothing a rule reads

behaviours.name: ids.sequential_survives_concurrent_writers
behaviours.what: a command that mints an id re-reads the plan and mints again when another writer takes it first, so concurrent writers do not serialise on the id

behaviours.name: ids.concurrent_snapshot_instability_is_retried
behaviours.what: an ID-creating mutation treats candidate-set instability during its pre-write plan snapshot as bounded contention, distinct from a file changed after it was read

behaviours.name: authoring.task_ids_preserve_cut_labels
behaviours.what: in-plan task creation and rekey refuse an id that would shadow a displayed cut label, before publishing any file

behaviours.name: rekey.surgical_yaml_scalars
behaviours.what: `rekey` treats a quoted task id or a block-list relationship member as one scalar and preserves the comments and bytes around it

behaviours.name: rekey.reports_moved_filename_links
behaviours.what: `rekey` includes repository text naming the old conventional `.md` filename in its possible-reference review list without rewriting it

behaviours.name: rekey.policy_cut_block_comments
behaviours.what: `rekey` preserves an inline comment on a `policy[].when.cut` block key while changing its exact milestone-id members

behaviours.name: rekey.relocation_late_failure_cleans_staging
behaviours.what: a late sibling-backup failure during `rekey` restores every original file and removes every unpublished staging file

behaviours.name: tui.layered_cell_scene_is_bounded_and_deterministic
behaviours.what: the multiscale semantic graph can be laid out as deterministic terminal-cell nodes, phase bands and exact routed edges under explicit work limits, with typed degradation, stable prior geometry and generation-safe fallback

behaviours.name: tui.layered_graph_is_a_semantic_ratatui_widget
behaviours.what: the TUI Graph destination paints the bounded layered scene as adaptive phase bands, semantic cards, ports and routed edges with cell-accurate hit targets, viewport accounting and an honest selectable fallback

behaviours.name: tui.selected_graph_card_is_one_continuous_surface
behaviours.what: a selected layered-graph task or aggregate card paints every visible interior cell with one coherent theme-selected style, including unused row suffixes and blank rows, without changing graph identity or hit geometry

behaviours.name: tui.layered_graph_navigation_is_semantic_and_reversible
behaviours.what: the layered Graph destination navigates actual dependency geometry and direct relations, drills and reverses plan/phase/milestone/task levels with exact session and contextual-return history, preserves explicit order, direction, density and scope policies, and keeps bounded off-view traversal typed

behaviours.name: graph.layered_scene_is_complete_or_fallback
behaviours.what: a layered scene is paintable only when every admitted edge, non-empty phase band and semantic identity has complete validated current geometry; any failure becomes an explained selectable fallback, and retained geometry is recovery input rather than current paint or hit state

behaviours.name: graph.layered_hardening_corpus_is_executable
behaviours.what: the shared layered graph runs one discoverable hostile corpus and every four-node DAG through deterministic cell geometry, proving exact edge provenance, phase containment, valid ports and routes, no overlap, typed feedback and total dependency accounting in both orientations

behaviours.name: graph.layered_routes_choose_low_bend_ports_within_crossing_budget
behaviours.what: layered routes may choose any valid node-boundary port when that reduces bends; on the matched crossing-heavy corpus both orientations retain exact monotone routes while producing no more unrelated-edge crossings than Lanes and at most 125 percent of its bends

behaviours.name: graph.layered_text_uses_the_shared_semantic_scene
behaviours.what: `graph --format text --layout layered` paints the same typed multiscale projection and validated terminal-cell scene as the TUI under explicit level, orientation, peer-order, detail, width and glyph policies; redirected bytes are deterministic and every omission is accounted while lanes remains an explicit compatibility layout

behaviours.name: graph.auto_text_orientation_prefers_a_scene_which_fits
behaviours.what: static layered text Auto orientation retains both validated direction candidates until the exact document width is known, chooses the best-quality complete scene which fits, and reports the smallest required width only when neither fits; explicitly forced directions and viewport-independent application/TUI Auto semantics are unchanged

behaviours.name: graph.text_defaults_to_layered_with_explicit_lane_compatibility
behaviours.what: `graph --format text` selects the shared Layered scene and therefore requires an exact width when redirected; `--layout lanes` retains the prior row-and-lane bytes, and JSON, Mermaid and DOT bytes and accepted controls do not change

behaviours.name: graph.attended_default_is_layered_and_redirected_default_is_mermaid
behaviours.what: an attended bare `graph` selects width-aware layered text, redirected bare `graph` retains deterministic Mermaid, and an explicit format remains authoritative in either environment

behaviours.name: graph.cell_routes_repair_terminal_border_collisions
behaviours.what: terminal-cell adaptation deterministically diverts an orthogonal route around unrelated painted card cells while preserving endpoints, monotone direction and complete edge identity; geometry which cannot be repaired still becomes an explained fallback

behaviours.name: graph.layered_phase_labels_are_horizontal_and_non_occluding
behaviours.what: layered phase labels in either orientation are horizontal top-border labels, so a top-to-bottom scene never overwrites a band edge or node card

behaviours.name: graph.aggregate_levels_are_bounded_and_continuable
behaviours.what: plan and phase aggregate levels apply a source-bound semantic node and edge window before cell layout, preserve exact raw-task and dependency accounting, and expose continuations which both the TUI and static text can traverse

behaviours.name: tui.external_observation_is_shutdown_cancellable
behaviours.what: periodic and focus-gain repository observations receive the worker cancellation token and yield at identified load boundaries, so graceful quit cannot wait for a newly in-flight observation after terminal restoration

behaviours.name: tui.simultaneous_resize_and_input_are_not_lost
behaviours.what: the Unix TUI polls terminal readiness level-triggered and consumes terminal input before a simultaneous resize notification, so an already queued key cannot be stranded after SIGWINCH

behaviours.name: tui.hidden_graph_resize_defers_reprojection
behaviours.what: terminal resize updates the future graph density without reprojecting or laying out a hidden Graph destination; the bounded scene is rebuilt from current size only when Graph becomes visible again

behaviours.name: tui.graph_fallback_paint_is_viewport_bounded
behaviours.what: the graph fallback caches complete-source extent when the projection changes and translates the visible row interval directly into a source-node slice, so steady-state paint work and allocation are bounded by the viewport rather than complete graph size

behaviours.name: tui.graph_selection_reuses_current_projection
behaviours.what: selecting a subject represented at a selection-independent plan or phase graph level updates selection and source-bound transition subjects in place, then refocuses retained cell geometry without repeating complete-source semantic projection; bounded detail levels still reproject around their new anchor

behaviours.name: tui.refresh_rebuilds_only_the_visible_projection
behaviours.what: refresh adopts the coherent shared snapshot and reconciles the visible destination plus shared work and inspector state; hidden Tasks, Graph and Reports projections defer source-sized work until route entry, where they rebuild from the adopted snapshot

commands.about: Capture a thought quickly without creating a task or graph node
commands.name: capture

commands.about: Review, amend, discard or restore versioned capture intake
commands.name: inbox

commands.about: Validate the plan. Fails on any error. Reads `.aplan.yml` if present; flags below override it
commands.name: check

commands.about: Resolve evidence against the git repository (L1/L2, and L3 with `--execute`). Unlike `check`, this opens the repo: a `commit` must exist and touch the task's `paths`, a `file` must exist at the cited rev, a `test` must be one the configured runner lists
commands.name: verify

commands.about: Inspect the exact evidence names configured test runners report
commands.name: test

commands.about: List tasks whose blockers are all `done`, best first
commands.name: ready

commands.about: Parked tasks whose `revisit_at` has arrived: a hand-off to a scheduler
commands.name: due

commands.about: Explain what is blocking a task: its own blockers, and any unfinished cut
commands.name: why

commands.about: What the plan says the next version must be
commands.name: version

commands.about: Explore the dependency graph as layered terminal text, or export it
commands.name: graph

commands.about: Open the interactive terminal interface
commands.name: tui

commands.about: Show one task whole: its fields, what it waits on and releases, and the findings currently attached to it
commands.name: show

commands.about: Explain one name from an explicit vocabulary
commands.name: explain

commands.about: Show one task's neighbourhood: what must precede it, and what it releases
commands.name: tree

commands.about: Measure how much of recent history each task's `paths` would match
commands.name: paths

commands.about: Report what each rule could actually have failed on
commands.name: vacuity

commands.about: Report live tasks that have sat unchanged, and which of them could start
commands.name: stale

commands.about: Report the deprecation runways this plan declares
commands.name: deprecations

commands.about: Record what this plan proved, bound to the commit it proved it at
commands.name: attest

commands.about: Write the agent contract this repository's policy implies
commands.name: export-agents-md

commands.about: Write the plan's statuses back into a `roadmap.json` contract
commands.name: export-roadmap-json

commands.about: Write the plan out in somebody else's shape
commands.name: export

commands.about: Check that a document names tasks that exist
commands.name: check-docs

commands.about: Roll the plan up by phase, or by `summary.group_by`: tasks, effort, and readiness
commands.name: summary

commands.about: Drop a task, or a whole cut, recording the decision rather than deleting the record of it. Refuses to revive anything already terminal
commands.name: drop

commands.about: Park existing todo work as one validated change. Records the reason in every task body; elapsed revisit time never authorizes an automatic unpark
commands.name: park

commands.about: Return parked work to `todo` as one validated change. Clears `revisit_at`, preserves body history and tags, and never bypasses graph blockers
commands.name: unpark

commands.about: Record who is working on a task, so two actors sharing a repository can see it. Linked worktrees contend on one private record in Git's common directory. Refuses to take a task somebody else holds unless `--from` names them
commands.name: claim

commands.about: Drop a local claim, naming its holder, time and origin. Anybody may run it, including for an id absent from this worktree, so an orphaned claim always has an explicit recovery path
commands.name: release

commands.about: Record that work on a task has started. The status is checked against the repository afterwards, so this is a statement `verify` can contradict rather than one it takes on trust
commands.name: start

commands.about: Record that work on a task has stopped, returning it to `todo`. Not a closure: nothing is claimed about the work, which is what `close` is for
commands.name: stop

commands.about: Move tasks between cuts, editing both milestones or neither
commands.name: mv

commands.about: Change a task's stable id and every structured reference to it as one guarded edit
commands.name: rekey

commands.about: Emit the plan's tasks as data, so a rollup this tool does not have is a `jq` line rather than a feature request. Carries what a rollup needs resolved: the cut a task belongs to, and whether it is ready
commands.name: tasks

commands.about: Show the critical path: the longest `effort_days`-weighted chain of dependent tasks. Advisory, never a gate
commands.name: critical-path

commands.about: Render the plan grouped by cut (the milestones): per-cut rollups, the critical path, and cross-cutting tasks. Advisory: it reports, and never fails a build
commands.name: roadmap

commands.about: Close a task: set it `done` and attach evidence, in place. With no `--evidence`, records the current `HEAD` commit
commands.name: close

commands.about: Repair a closed task's evidence: add, replace or remove a citation, in place, without reopening it
commands.name: amend

commands.about: File the successor to a closed task whose traced outcome no longer holds, and re-stamp the closed one as reviewed
commands.name: supersede

commands.about: Add or remove dependency edges: repeat `--after`, or use `dep apply` for mixed multi-target additions and removals against one final graph
commands.name: dep

commands.about: Add, remove or rename a tag: `tag add A cli`, `tag rm A cli`, and `tag rename epic-a epic-b` across every task that carries it
commands.name: tag

commands.about: Import proposals from another tool's format into `aplan` tasks. Lossy by design, and says so: every field the task model cannot hold is reported
commands.name: import

commands.about: Preview or apply one explicit blueprint file as one guarded graph
commands.name: blueprint

commands.about: Scaffold a new task file: the next id in this plan's own convention, the fields `check` needs, and a body to fill in. It fills in nothing it cannot know, so a new task carries no estimate and no evidence unless you give them. `--from <file>` adds every task a file names instead, as one change
commands.name: add

commands.about: Run an MCP server over stdio, exposing a deliberately small tool set (`identity`, `ready`, `why`, `check`, `verify`, `add`, `show`, `dep`, `close`, `claim`, `release`, `start`, `stop`) to an agent. `close` goes through the same evidence gate as the CLI, in both directions: an agent cannot close through MCP what it could not close here, and is not refused what this command records
commands.name: mcp

commands.about: Scaffold a starter `.aplan.yml`, refusing to overwrite an existing one
commands.name: init

commands.about: Print this tool's facts as JSON: its rules, output formats, commands, and evidence kinds, generated from the code (the source for `facts.json`)
commands.name: facts

commands.about: Print the JSON Schema derived from the Rust types
commands.name: schema

mcp_tools.description: Name the build of this server: its version, the commit it was built from, and the digests of its capability document and its own image. Asking an installed CLI does not answer this -- a configured MCP process may be a different executable, which is how a pilot spent a pass on a defect the checkout had already fixed. Needs no plan and no repository.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_identity

mcp_tools.description: List tasks whose blockers are all done, so an agent can pick real work.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_ready

mcp_tools.description: Explain what is blocking a task: its own blockers, and any unfinished cut, without expanding that cut's membership. Pass `all` for the complete transitive closure; every answer names its `traversal`.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_why

mcp_tools.description: Validate the plan and return its diagnostics, and `denied`: whether this plan fails the build under the repository's warning policy. Hermetic: no git, no network.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_check

mcp_tools.description: Resolve the plan's evidence against the repository (L1/L2): a cited commit must be reachable from HEAD and touch the task's `paths`, a cited file must exist. Opens git and may run configured discovery/check providers, but never executes a cited test.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_verify

mcp_tools.description: Create a task with an explicit id and phase, or mint the next id in this plan's own convention (including its configured ULID strategy) and derive the phase from its cut. It accepts live initial states, every creation-time relationship, revisit scheduling and version impact; terminal history uses the CLI's evidence-resolving manifest ledger. With `members`, both identity fields are required: create that milestone and move existing live work from its source cuts in one guarded batch. Refuses before writing what `check` would reject after, by running the rules on the plan this would produce; what it would only warn about is named in `notes` instead.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_add

mcp_tools.description: One task whole: its `paths`, `traces` and `evidence`, which no other tool returns, plus what the graph resolves (its cut, whether it is ready, what it waits on and what it releases) and every finding attached to it. Reads repository-backed evidence and retained typed provider observations without starting configured processes; `aplan_verify` explicitly refreshes providers.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_show

mcp_tools.description: Add or remove one dependency edge: `after` is the task that must finish first. `blocked_by` is the only ordering the model has and it was writable only at creation, so re-sequencing meant editing files by hand. Refuses before writing what `check` would reject after: a cycle, an id that does not exist, a cancelled blocker, or a done task acquiring an unfinished one. A milestone's `blocked_by` is which tasks are in that cut rather than what it comes after, so editing that is refused here and belongs to `aplan mv`.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_dep

mcp_tools.description: Close a task with evidence, resolved at L2 before it is written: a cited commit must be reachable from HEAD and touch the task's `paths`, a cited file must exist, and a cited test must be one a configured runner lists. Refuses exactly what the CLI refuses; evidence is a citation to be resolved, never a score the caller asserts. This agent tool never runs a test; it never starts `test.run` or `test.batch`. Focused L3 closure is an explicit trusted CLI or interactive action. It never fetches a url, and whatever nothing here could check is named in `unchecked` rather than left looking like a pass. `aplan_verify` resolves the whole plan.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_close

mcp_tools.description: Record that you are working on a task, so other agents sharing this Git repository and all of its linked worktrees can see the same local ephemeral claim. It never edits the task or its durable `owner`. Two agents cannot both be told they hold one task: the common-directory record is a compare-and-swap. Taking a held task needs `from` naming the displaced holder. Labels are attribution, not authentication; the response includes time, origin, source and coordination scope.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_claim

mcp_tools.description: Drop a claim, reporting whose it was. Any caller may release, because a claim lasts until it is released or taken over and an abandoned one has to be clearable by somebody else. A missing task's orphaned local claim can still be released explicitly. Releasing a visible task nobody holds changes nothing and says so.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_release

mcp_tools.description: Record that work on a task has begun, setting `in_progress`. A claim rather than a proof, and checked like one: `aplan_verify` reports `APLAN053` where the repository holds nothing matching the task's `paths`, so a status nobody acted on does not pass as progress. Refuses a task that is already terminal, because nothing reopens finished work.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_start

mcp_tools.description: Record that work on a task has stopped, returning it to `todo`. Not a closure: it claims nothing about what was done, which is what `aplan_close` is for. Refuses a task that is not `in_progress`, since there is then nothing to stop.
mcp_tools.name: aplan_stop

rules.title: frontmatter parses and satisfies the schema
task ids are unique
blocked_by references a task that exists
the dependency graph is acyclic
done carries at least one piece of evidence
no task blocks itself
a done task does not depend on an unfinished one
traces anchors resolve to a real heading or node
active tasks carry an effort estimate
a note used as evidence carries a date
commit evidence resolves to an immutable commit reachable from HEAD
commit evidence touches at least one of the task's paths
test evidence names a test the runner can find
test evidence names a test that passes
file evidence resolves at the cited rev
url evidence answers when it is checked
done evidence meets the configured minimum strength
a closed task's traced section is unchanged since closure
a task's paths globs each match at least one tracked file, once it cites evidence
a live task is not blocked by a dropped one
a milestone has members and carries no effort or paths
every task is a member of exactly one cut, or is tagged cross-cutting
a done task's path-checkable evidence can actually be path-checked
a done task's commit evidence is about that task, not mostly about other work
a cited test belongs to the part of the repository this task's `paths` cover
a tag that looks like a member of a declared family is one
a cancelled cut's members are cancelled too
a done task stamps every trace that can be stamped
a declared tag family is carried by at least one task
a task carries the number of members a declared family requires
file evidence names a file inside the task's paths
a task's paths entries are globs this tool can compile
a prefer_after entry names a task that can actually be preferred
a traces target outside this repository is declared as external
commit evidence names a commit that did work, not a merge
a configured test runner lists at least one test, or says it expects none
a test that passed under `--execute` is distinguishable from one the runner never ran
a `done` task has answered the acceptance criteria its own body states
a `done` task has not ticked a prompt this tool wrote as though it were a criterion
a task declares each `paths` entry once
the generated `AGENTS.md` block says what this repository's policy says
a `revisit_at` names a real instant, on a task that is parked
a live task carries the scaffold's own prompt beside the criteria its author wrote
a closed task claims less of the released version than its level implies, without saying why
a live task's traced section is unchanged since the task was last touched
a done task's ratifiers are done
a `contains` names a milestone that exists, and closes no loop
the released version has moved as far as the closed tasks require
the artifact agrees with what the plan claims about compatibility
a recorded `version` is on a release, and is a version this tool can read
a tag is not one edit from a word that changes what this tool does
`cross-cutting` is not on a task that is a member of a cut
a task that is `in_progress` has something in the repository to show for it
a closed task's mutable file evidence is covered by a current fingerprint
captured dates are used only for authored note evidence
a task's owner belongs to the declared owner vocabulary
every inbox entry is one canonical, valid and cross-record-consistent V1 capture
